title: Rare complication: no-reflow after simulated PCI

symptoms: The patient initially presents with an acute coronary syndrome; during the simulated intervention, epicardial anatomy appears improved but myocardial perfusion remains poor.
This is a complication branch attached to an ACS case, not a stand-alone diagnostic presentation.
history: Large thrombus burden in the fictional culprit lesion
medications: Periprocedural medication record is intentionally incomplete; learner must request reconciliation rather than infer doses
presentation.vitals: Before event: HR 88 bpm, BP 118/72 mmHg. After event: BP trends down and ischemic discomfort persists in the deterministic event timeline.
presentation.initial_ecg_summary: Persistent ST elevation/ischemic changes after simulated epicardial opening.
presentation.initial_troponin_summary: Troponin trend expected to rise in the infarction context; no single biomarker can diagnose no-reflow. Hemoglobin, renal function and electrolytes reviewed for safety.
presentation.notice: Synthetic educational scenario only; pending clinical review. Simulation tier is not a validated clinical risk score.
